data.title: SA Asks: What's the best gold play right now for investors?
data.description:
What's the best gold play right now for investors?

Seeking Alpha analysts Andrew Hecht, Brett Aschcroft Green, and Eugenio Catone weigh in.

Andrew Hecht: Gold is ugly, along with other markets that appear to be undergoing a risk-off phase. Picking bottoms is dangerous, as prices can fall to unreasonable, illogical, and irrational levels before finding bottoms.

All the analysts who were forecasting prices at $6,000 earlier this year again have egg on their face. Remember, they were the same analysts who never forecast gold reaching the level it rose to in late January 2026.

While I still believe gold will find a higher low, the next long-term support is the psychological $3,000 level. However, technical support for the bull market that began in 1999 is at the December 2023 high of $2,130.20 per ounce, more than $1,385 below last Friday's settlement price on Nov. 20. Central banks will continue to add to reserves at lower prices. That said, sentiment has taken a significant hit as gold has fallen by more than $2,000 per ounce from the Jan. 29, 2026, record high.

As a long-term investor, I would add to long positions by buying physical gold or SPDR Gold Shares ETF , the most liquid gold ETF that holds physical gold bullion. In late November 2026, gold and all precious metals remain falling knives, so be careful.

(Andrew Hecht leads the SA investing group The Hecht Commodity Report.)

Brett Aschcroft Green: The recent sell-off in gold could create an opportunity, as the metal may eventually represent a flight-to-safety asset and could be boosted by rate cuts if inflation subsides. I recently covered a few metals funds, which included a physical gold ETF, the SPDR Gold Shares ETF ; a large-cap miner fund, the VanEck Gold Miners ETF ; and a junior miner fund, the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF .

In the event of a sell-off, I’d be more inclined to go with the actual metals rather than the mining stocks.

Eugenio Catone: As I expressed in a recent article, the AI sell-off has led investors to sell liquid assets like gold to face margin calls. Since leverage is still high in the financial system, I expect a further drop in gold prices, at least until $3,400 per ounce, which is where the next strong volumetric support lies.

So, in my opinion, the best play here is to just wait until the dust settles ($3,400 per ounce) and buy a liquid ETC on gold for the long term. In this period, I would avoid miners as they are subject to operating leverage, something that becomes a major headwind when gold is in a sharp downward trend.

data.title: Bitcoin whales pile into BTC despite shrinking profit cushion
data.description:
Bitcoin whales are bucking the years-long trend of trimming their balances toward the end of the year. Instead, they are accumulating the cryptocurrency despite falling prices and dwindling unrealized profits.

According to onchain analytics firm CryptoQuant, whales added about 121,000 Bitcoin to their holdings between Sept. 30 and Nov. 21, taking their combined balance to nearly 2.95 million BTC, despite a price decline of nearly 30% over the same period.

CryptoQuant defines whales as addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC. Unrealized profits across addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have shrunk 81% to $23.8 billion from $124.7 billion on Sept. 30.

The report, supported by crypto lending platform CoinRabbit, notes that whales have historically reduced their holdings toward the end of the year in both bull and bear markets. Since 2017, whale balances have declined in seven of the nine previous fourth quarters, with 2019 and 2020 being the only exceptions.

Meanwhile, dolphins, a term referring to addresses holding between 100 and 1,000 BTC, have slightly reduced their holdings. The group shed about 15,169 BTC, representing 0.28% of its holdings.

Bitcoin loans may be taking the place of sales

The accumulation comes as Bitcoin has lost about 32% of its value since the beginning of the year, with the cryptocurrency trading at around $59,750 at 6:45 p.m. UTC on Friday, according to TradingView data. The report notes that borrowing against Bitcoin holdings may be allowing some large investors to access liquidity without selling their assets.

According to CryptoQuant, among CoinRabbit users with more than $100,000 in loans, the number of Bitcoin-backed loans increased by 298.9% month-on-month in October, while total loan volume fell by 16.2%.

The pattern contrasts with October 2025, when the number of Bitcoin-backed loans fell by 3.7% but total loan volume increased by 122.8%.

CryptoQuant suggested that the shift toward more frequent but smaller loans could indicate that large holders are borrowing to raise cash instead of selling Bitcoin.

Crypto tax firm Summ suggested the shift could also be linked to the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). Since January, participating jurisdictions have begun requiring crypto exchanges and other service providers to collect users’ transaction data for tax authorities, with the first international exchanges of tax-related information expected in 2027.

Summ CEO Shane Brunette said holding BTC and borrowing against it are rational responses “to a world where every sale is visible.”

data.title: Precious Metals Rally as AI Trade Revives Risk Appetite — Update
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni and Adam Whittaker

Precious-metal prices surged Friday as investors returned to the artificial-intelligence trade and global stocks rebounded, boosting risk appetite and easing pressure on assets that had been sold to meet liquidity needs.

Copper futures rose 3.4% Friday to $5.5170 a pound.

The rally also lifted mining stocks in London, with the sector leading gains on the FTSE 100. Friday's advance follows a challenging period for mining companies, whose shares have come under pressure as metal prices weakened and concerns about the AI trade weighed on investor sentiment.

Silver and gold miner Fresnillo shares rose 4.8%, while its peer Endeavour Mining gained 3.1%. Copper producer Antofagasta climbed 4.4%. Diversified miners Glencore and Anglo American, both with significant exposure to copper, advanced 4.3% and 3.8%, respectively. Valterra Platinum's London-listed shares gained 7.8%.

"Beyond the technical nature of the rebound, the recovery also highlights the role of precious metals as an ATM in times of market stress," analysts at Saxo Bank said. "With AI-related technology stocks rebounding and broader risk appetite improving, the queue at the cash machine appears to be thinning, easing the liquidity-driven selling pressure."

Still, the broader macroeconomic backdrop remains challenging. Traders are pricing in a quarter-point rate hike at the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting in December, while attention is also turning to whether the U.S. central bank will signal further monetary tightening for 2027.

Higher interest rates can weigh on nonyielding assets such as gold and silver by making interest-bearing investments relatively more attractive.

data.title: Apple faces countersuit from OpenAI for stealing trade secrets - FT
data.description:
OpenAI has launched a new legal action against Apple , accusing the iPhone maker of stealing trade secrets and blocking access to hardware suppliers, reported the Financial Times on Friday.

OpenAI filed the lawsuit in a California court on Friday, according to the report.

OpenAI claimed that Apple is using its “size and wealth to forestall competition,” including threatening suppliers that might work on its new devices, alleging a “wide variety of unlawful, unfair, and tortious conduct,” the Financial Times report added.

The ChatGPT maker and Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comments.

The report also stated that OpenAI accused Apple of “coercing and threatening” suppliers that are also working with the ChatGPT maker.

OpenAI also reportedly said that one of its former employees who returned to Apple shared details about its product plans and suppliers. According to the Financial Times, OpenAI claimed that Apple encouraged its employees to store corporate files on their personal devices and cloud storage accounts.

The new development comes after Apple, in July, reportedly sent legal letters to former employees who now work for OpenAI, with the tech giant alleging that OpenAI is stealing trade secrets.

Apple alleged OpenAI used former and current Apple employees to steal confidential hardware designs and confidential information of unreleased technologies, processes and products. It also alleges that the misconduct was orchestrated by OpenAI's leadership.

Last year, OpenAI also acquired io, the AI startup led by Apple’s former design chief Sir Jony Ive, for $6.4 billion, creating a new source of tension between the two companies.

The continuing legal battle will further deteriorate the relationship between the two companies, who once partnered in June 2024 to integrate ChatGPT into iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. Apple also worked with OpenAI to help upgrade its Siri assistant.

data.title: Dollar set for weekly gain as risk appetite returns
data.description:
Key points:
  • Australian dollar rebounds from Wednesday's near one-year low as sentiment improves
  • China's steps to support equities add to broader market risk appetite
  • Fed funds futures imply near-certain December hike and sizable odds of another in January

By Karen Brettell

Improving risk appetite on Friday bolstered risk-sensitive currencies including the Australian dollar, while the US dollar was on track for a modest weekly gain.

Wall Street's main indexes ended higher on Friday and posted weekly gains as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday and flocked to hard-hit AI-linked shares. Efforts by China to shore up its stock market also boosted sentiment.

"A dip-buying recovery in tech stocks is lifting risk appetite across markets," said Elias Haddad, global head of markets strategy at Brown Brothers Harriman.

The US currency has benefited from safe-haven demand amid volatile equity markets, but it is also sensitive to capital flows to the AI trade, which has made it difficult at times to parse market moves.

“FX markets have shaken off their fixation on energy markets, replacing it, for now, with a focus on equities,” said Daragh Maher, head of digital assets research and senior FX strategist at HSBC.

“This creates a headache. The USD’s relationship with equities is unreliable, caught between its safe-haven role and its appeal as a proxy for US exceptionalism. The same equity signal could prompt very different FX responses,” he said.

The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.25% to 104.04, with the euro down 0.31% at $1.0933. The US currency is headed for a weekly gain of 0.2%.

The Australian dollar strengthened 0.18% versus the greenback to $0.6644, recovering from an almost one-year low reached on Wednesday.

FED TO CONTINUE HIKING

With US growth remaining strong and inflation still elevated, traders are pricing in continued rate hikes from the Federal Reserve, which has also supported the US currency.

Fed funds futures traders are pricing in 99% odds of a hike in December and a 64% chance of an additional increase in January, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool.

Key data releases next week, including November’s jobs report, will be evaluated for further clues on likely Fed policy.

Data on Friday showed that the US trade deficit in goods widened sharply in October as an AI infrastructure buildout boosted imports to a record high, potentially putting trade on course to again subtract from economic growth in the fourth quarter.

DOLLAR/YEN 160 LEVEL BACK IN FOCUS

Against the Japanese yen , the dollar strengthened 0.16% to 159.51, amid concerns about another round of Japanese intervention.

Data showed that annual core inflation in Tokyo accelerated in November at the fastest pace in 16 months, bolstering the case for an interest rate hike as soon as next month.

"The yen is understandably weaker today given the strong rebound in risk that has helped lift US Treasury bond yields," said Derek Halpenny, strategist at MUFG. "Better risk conditions could quickly bring back focus on intervention, especially if we get a hawkish hike from the FOMC on December 9."

In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 1.38% to $59,922.

data.title: Canadian dollar holds on to weekly gain as investors bet on December rate hike
data.description:
By Fergal Smith

The Canadian dollar remained on track to snap a three-week losing streak against the US dollar on Friday as investors stuck with bets the Bank of Canada would raise interest rates further next month.

The loonie was trading nearly unchanged at 1.4245 per US dollar, or 70.20 US cents, after moving in a range of 1.4224 to 1.4260.

  • For the week, the currency was up 0.7%, after a speech by Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem led to increased expectations for a December rate hike

  • "Comments from Governor Macklem this week underscored the Bank of Canada’s concerns about building inflation pressures across the economy," Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret, strategists at Scotiabank, said in a note

  • "Second round effects will add to inflation persistence and even if somewhat lower oil prices mean that inflation will not rise as much as policymakers had previously expected," the strategists said

  • Investors see a 77% chance the BoC will raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% next month after the central bank tightened in October for the first time in three years (0#CADIRPR)

  • Canadian third-quarter GDP data, due on Monday, could guide rate hike expectations. Economists expect growth to slow to an annualized pace of 1.5% from 3.3% in the second quarter

  • The price of oil, one of Canada's major exports, pulled back from an earlier 10-day high. US crude oil futures were trading 0.8% lower $83 a barrel, while the US dollar notched gains against a basket of major currencies

  • Canadian bond yields rose across the curve, with the market tracking moves in US Treasuries as technology stocks rebounded. The 10-year (CA10YT=RR) was up 5.7 basis points at 3.699%

  • Investors had considered whether recent volatility in technology stocks could tighten financial conditions and persuade the Federal Reserve to hold off from multiple interest rate hikes

data.title: Gold pares gains as Fed hike risks linger, eyes first weekly rise in three weeks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold pares gains after jumping over 3% earlier in the session
  • Spot silver up nearly 5%, off $38.18/oz lows hit on Wednesday
  • Gold, silver, platinum eye first weekly gain in three weeks

By Sherin Sans

Gold pared gains on Friday as a firm US dollar, rising Treasury yields and a hawkish Federal Reserve outlook kept investors cautious, but bullion remained on track for its first weekly gain in three as bargain-buying lifted prices from a 15-month low hit earlier this week.

Spot gold rose 2.1% to $3,639.61 per ounce by 2:01 p.m. ET (1901 GMT), having risen more than 3% earlier in the session. The metal was on track for a weekly gain of nearly 3% after posting losses in the previous two weeks.

US gold futures for December delivery gained 2.9% to $3,637.60 per ounce.

"This recent bounce looks more like short-covering/profit-taking than a change in trend. The Fed is still hiking, real yields are high and the dollar is near multi-month highs. Until one of those shifts, rallies toward $3,750–$3,800 could attract sellers," said Zain Vawda, market analyst at Audacity Capital.

The dollar was still close to its highest level in 22 months, making dollar-priced bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies, while the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield rose and was off its recent lows.

Gold fell to its lowest level since late August 2025, at $3,426.35 per ounce, on Wednesday after strong US inflation data boosted expectations that the Fed will keep raising interest rates next month and again in early 2027.

"A return to $5,000 is possible, but not in the first half of the year. Gold needs the Fed to stop hiking and the dollar to roll over. If that happens by mid-2027, a recovery toward $4,500 is realistic," Vawda added.

Rising interest rates diminish gold's appeal by boosting returns on competing interest-bearing assets.

Meanwhile, physical gold demand in key Asian hubs improved this week, with jewellery and investment buying picking up in India, while strong retail purchases in China kept local premiums firm.

Spot silver climbed 4.7% to $43.44 per ounce, platinum gained 2.3% to $1,319.96 per ounce and palladium rose 1.8% to $889.01.

All three metals were poised for weekly gains.

data.title: Malibu Boats Agrees in Principle to $300,000 SEC Penalty
data.description:
Malibu Boats reached an agreement in principle to pay a $300,000 civil penalty to resolve an SEC investigation.

Key Highlights:

  • The investigation concerns statements about channel inventory in fiscal 2023 and the first quarter of fiscal 2024.
  • It also concerns alleged failure to disclose a deteriorating relationship with Tommy’s Boats from December 2023 or January 2024 until April 2024.
  • The proposed resolution includes a cease-and-desist order and requires definitive documentation and SEC approval.
  • Malibu Boats does not expect the resolution to materially affect its financial position.

data.title: Trutankless®, Inc. Strengthens Balance Sheet, Converts Approximately $5 Million in Notes into Equity
data.description:
Conversion eliminates more than $400,000 in annual interest expense as nine-month net sales rise 146% to a record

SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Trutankless®, Inc. (), the Company known for its GEN3-series of smart electric tankless water heaters, today announced that its noteholders have converted approximately $5,000,000 in notes into equity. The conversion eliminates more than $400,000 in annual interest expense on the notes. Additional details are included in a Current Report on Form 8-K that the Company filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on November 24, 2026.

The conversion builds on prior debt-to-equity conversions, including approximately $3 million in April 2024, and continues the Company's plan to strengthen its capital structure while aligning investors with the growth of the brand. For plumbing technicians and wholesale partners, that means a manufacturer with more room to invest in inventory, training and support.

The conversion comes as demand accelerates. The Company reported that net sales for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, rose 146% to a record $1,841,929, compared to $748,491 for the same period in 2025. Third quarter net sales grew 62% year over year to $362,790.

Trutankless® continues to expand its wholesale distribution partner network and contractor relationships nationwide, with particularly strong momentum in Arizona, Texas and Florida. Its 14,000-square-foot North Phoenix facility, opened in October 2025, brings production, engineering, installer training and distribution under one roof. In April, it launched the GEN3 Commercial 208V unit, engineered for condominiums, multi-family housing, salons, restaurants, fitness studios and other light commercial settings.

GEN3+, the next generation of the Trutankless® smart electric tankless water heater, is now in production and shipping. The wireless connected unit works with the Trutankless® connected app for homeowners and the Trutankless® Pro app and Pro dashboard for plumbing professionals, all now in beta. The Company plans to share full GEN3+ details in December.

"This conversion strengthens our balance sheet and lets us put more of our resources behind growth," said Guy Newman, CEO of Trutankless®. "Nine-month sales are up 146%, our distributor and contractor network keeps growing, and our Phoenix facility gives us room to scale. With GEN3+ now shipping and our Pro app and Pro dashboard in beta, we are giving plumbing professionals the tools to support every system they install."

About Trutankless®

Trutankless® is the premier brand in electric tankless water heating. The award-winning brand's GEN3 and GEN3+ lineup delivers endless, on-demand hot water in a sleek, space-saving design for homes, condos, multi-family and light commercial spaces.

The Trutankless® connected app is designed to put performance insights and preventative maintenance alerts in the hands of homeowners and plumbing pros, keeping every system running at peak performance, maximizing energy efficiency and extending its service life.

Trutankless® products are sold through plumbing wholesale distributors and dealers nationwide. Founded in 2008, Trutankless®, Inc. () is headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona. Learn more at www.trutankless.com.

data.title: Researchers Identify New Depression Subtype Linked To Body's Internal Clock
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Researchers have identified a new type of depression called circadian depression, which may affect about one in four people with severe, recurring or long-term depression.

'Our research has identified circadian depression as a new subtype, affecting around a quarter of people in our study into those with severe, recurrent or persistent depression,' said first author Emiliana Tonini from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Center.

This type of depression is linked to the body's internal clock, which controls when we sleep and wake up. People with circadian depression are more likely to stay up late at night, sleep longer than usual, feel tired even after getting enough sleep and experience more severe depression symptoms. Their symptoms may also change depending on the season.

The discovery came from an analysis of medical and genetic data from more than 10,000 Australians with depression. Researchers found that 2,604 people, or nearly 25% of the participants, showed signs of circadian depression.

Published in the British Journal of Psychiatry, the findings suggested that medications commonly used for depression may be less effective in people with circadian depression. They may also experience more side effects from these treatments.

'Because circadian depression is linked to people's internal body clock, treatments targeting the circadian rhythm, such as light therapy and melatonin, may be much more relevant, and clinicians should reach for these much earlier in people with this presentation,' co-senior author Jacob Crouse said.

'For those who find that antidepressants are not working for them, it is important to speak to your clinician for advice about your individual circumstances.'

Identifying circadian depression early could help doctors choose treatments that better suit each patient. This may be especially important for younger people, who could otherwise spend a long time trying different medicines that may not provide enough relief.

data.title: Soybeans Close Week With Solid Gains — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

  • Soybeans for January Delivery rose 1.8% Friday on the Chicago Board of Trade to $12.66 1/4 a bushel, with support from strong soybean meal exports and a recovering Brazilan real.
  • Corn for March delivery rose 1.4% to $4.63 a bushel.
  • Wheat for March delivery rose 0.6% to $5.91 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

Europe Calling: While U.S. soybean export sales fell last week, soybean cake and meal sales jumped to 543,500 metric tons from 198,100 tons the week before, with Spain, Italy and Poland among the principal buyers. With three of the top four buyers being EU countries, the purchases could show that diversification is on importers' minds as EU deforestation regulation is set to kick in at the end of the year, Mike Castle of StoneX said in a note.

"While a single week's sales data are not sufficient to establish a trend, the U.S. is widely viewed as one of the best-positioned suppliers to capture incremental EU demand due to its relatively favorable traceability and deforestation profile compared to South American competitors," he said.

Export Sales: Corn export sales for the 2026/27 marketing year totaled 1.93 million metric tons in the week ended Nov. 19, up 21% from the week before, the USDA reprted. Wheat sales for 2026/27 rose 64% to 564,700 tons, while soybean sales fell 50% to 755,800 tons for 2026/27, with an additional 2,200 tons sold for 2027/28.

Analyst estimates in a Wall Street Journal survey ranged from 250,000 tons to 550,000 tons for wheat, from 700,000 tons to 1.77 million tons for corn, and from 800,000 tons to 1.6 million tons for soybeans.

Netherlands Buying: The USDA reported sales of 132,000 metric tons of soybeans for delivery to the Netherlands during the 2026/27 marketing year.

INSIGHT

Market Friendly: The Brazilian real is recovering against the U.S. dollar after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva appointed the chairman of Bradesco Bank as his next finance minister, a decision seen as market friendly. The slide in the real following Lula's surprise re-election win last month put downward pressure on U.S. soybean prices on concerns that Brazilian exporters would have a large exchange advantage over U.S. producers.

Back From Oversold: Corn futures are starting to correct from an oversold condition, Doug Bergman of RCM Alternatives said in a note. A higher bean market and limited farmer selling interest have helped the market add value," he said. "The current supply/demand outlook is expected to limit downside risk with prices seen working higher into the winter."

AHEAD

-The USDA will release its weekly Grain Export Inspections report at 11 a.m. ET Monday.

-The USDA will release its weekly Crop Progress report at 4 p.m. ET Monday.

-The USDA will release its monthly Grain Crushings report at 3 p.m. ET Tuesday

data.title: Shopify Stocks Jump 6.05% as Record Online Holiday Spending Kicks Off
data.description:
Shopify shares jumped 6.05% to $141.47 at 10:35 a.m. ET on Friday, November 27, as early Black Friday data pointed to strong online spending. The Canada-based company sells storefront, checkout and payments software to merchants, and TradingKey linked the move to early holiday merchandise-volume momentum, Shop Pay adoption and demand for its AI merchant tools.

Adobe data cited by ROIC shows U.S. consumers spent $7.1 billion online on Thanksgiving Day, up 10.4%, with Black Friday projected at $12.9 billion. In Toronto, Shopify gained 5.6% and led Canadian tech higher, The Globe and Mail reported. The risks have not gone away: TradingKey flagged conservative fourth-quarter gross-margin guidance, European GMV growth slowing to 33% from above 40%, and a forward P/E above 65 times, while Cantor Fitzgerald cut its target to $150.

The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 87/100, with a strong balance sheet and momentum but profitability as the softer spot. The GF Value of $166.40 implies a 15.0% discount, which GuruFocus calls modestly undervalued, yet at more than 65 times forward earnings that gap closes only if holiday volume turns into margin. The 6.05% jump also put Shopify's $182 billion market value back in play for momentum buyers. The next test is Cyber Monday, then the fourth-quarter report, where gross margin will show whether the holiday rush paid off.

data.title: Gold Soars As Trump's Stance On Diplomacy In Iran Crisis Clouds Fed Rate Hike Concerns
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Gold prices have surged on Friday, rebounding from recent losses as near-term war concerns eased after U.S. President Donald Trump prepares to give an opportunity for Iran to come up with a deal while continuing U.S. rate hike expectations capped the gains.

Of note, markets remained closed yesterday on account of the Thanksgiving Day holiday.

Front Month Comex Gold for January delivery has soared by $109.70 (or 3.09%) to $3,661.10 per troy ounce.

Front Month Comex Silver for January delivery has catapulted by $3.257 (or 8.09%) to $43.500 per troy ounce.

Ahead of December 8-9 meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve, market participants are focused on the next week's labor market data, including the key nonfarm payrolls report that is due on December 4.

Automatic Data Processing's private payrolls report is slated to be released on Wednesday, with weekly jobless claims on Thursday. The numbers could provide more clues on how the Fed may charter its trajectory on interest rates.

Currently, traders are betting on a 98.90% chance of the Fed instituting a 25-basis-point interest rate hike, according to the CME Group FedWatch tool.

Economists are of the view that if the data indicates strong economic growth, an interest rate raise could be inevitable.

U.S. technology stocks underwent heavy pressure over the past few days due to concerns among investors over the hyper-sized spendings on artificial intelligence related infrastructure building.

The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as the Chief Executive Officer of Nvidia offered only a short-lived breather as doubts over the return on AI-linked investments returned to markets.

Today, as investors re-assessed concerns over the profitability in super-sized AI spending, technology stocks recovered from some of their losses.

U.S. President Donald Trump stated that he had a discussion with Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Trump remarked that any future strikes against Iran would target Iran's Pickaxe Mountain, a location suspected to be Iran's underground nuclear facility.

Trump, however, stressed that he wanted to give Iran another chance to change course. Repeating his claims that U.S. forces have degraded Iran's military capabilities, Trump stated that he is giving Iran a chance to get smart.

Trump warned that Iran could strike European targets, a nuclear-armed Iran could trigger a nuclear holocaust in the Middle East and added that it cannot be allowed to have a nuclear weapon.

Two days before, under Section 301, the U.S. administration announced a fresh wave of tariffs on several countries including China, the European Union, and 12 other jurisdictions comprising Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan. The move follows an investigation into their trade practices.

The findings, according to White House, revealed that these countries subsidize heavily in favor of their domestic manufacturers and encourages exports to the U.S., which in turn cripples the U.S. manufacturers from doing their businesses. The levies take effect from January 2027.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer remarked that these new taxes would create a level playing field for the U.S. businesses.

Analysts are of the view that these tariffs could create friction between the U.S. and China, which is the largest competitor for the U.S. in the race for domination in artificial intelligence.

According to the World Gold Council's market update released on November 17, capitalizing on the recent slump in gold prices, China's central bank increased its reserves by adding 26 tonnes of gold in October.

China's official gold holdings reached 2,435 tonnes at the end of October.

Today, the WTI crude oil for December was last seen trading, down by $0.85 (or 1.02%), at $82.83 per barrel.

Today, the U.S. dollar index was last seen trading at 104.02, up by 0.36 (or 0.35%) today.

data.title: ANT Stock Ends First Full Week Of Trading Around 11% Above IPO Price: Lockup Expiry, Nasdaq 100 Entry Loom
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic stock ended its first full week of trading at a valuation of about $1.7 trillion after dipping below its offering price earlier in the week. 
  • Up to 303 million more ANT shares are slated to become eligible for sale on December 15.
  • Strong demand for tools like Claude Code and an $81 billion revenue run rate help offset investor worries over nearly $901 billion in capex commitments.

Anthropic PBC (ANT) share price pushed past their $83 initial public offering price on Friday, ending its first full week of trading higher.

The stock gained about 11% from its IPO price in the holiday-shortened week ending November 27. On Friday, the stock also hit its highest intraday price since Monday, snapping a two-day run of finishes below the IPO level as wider market risk appetite improved across tech stocks after the nearly month-long Nvidia (NVDA)-led selloff.

The Invesco QQQ ETF (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq 100 index, ended the week about 6.6% higher.

Valuation Pullback And Offering Mechanics

Friday's advance placed Anthropic's market value at roughly $1.3 trillion, well off the more than $2 trillion peak it reached during its November 19 debut when shares briefly hit $115.10 before pulling back.

The bumpy opening stretch has prompted questions from some market watchers about how the offering was handled. Critics have pointed to the decision allowing underwriting banks to exercise the over-allotment option right after the first day rather than holding that cushion in reserve to help steady the stock.

Attention has also centered on insider share supply under Anthropic's multi-stage lockup schedule. According to its prospectus, up to 315 million insider shares became eligible for release on day one.

Upcoming Share Releases

Another 303 million shares are scheduled to clear lockup restrictions on December 15, per the offering documents. At the same time, major benchmarks such as the Nasdaq 100 could add Anthropic later in December, a potential catalyst that could bring passive index fund demand.

In pitching the offering to investors, leadership led by CEO Dario Amodei leaned on rapid uptake of products including Claude Code, its software-engineering agent, alongside an $81 billion annualized revenue pace at the end of October. That momentum helped calm down some investor anxiety around the roughly $901 billion in committed expenditures stretching through 2045.

ANT Stock: Retail View 

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits towards Anthropic dropped to ‘neutral’ from ‘bullish’ a day ago and from’extremely bullish’ a week ago. Message volumes around the stock also eased to ‘high’ from ‘extremely high’ levels a week ago.

ANT stock gained about 2.5% this week.

Orexo AB (publ) (“Orexo” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq Stockholm: ORX) today announces the outcome of the rights issue of approximately 253 MSEK announced on 6 October 2026 (the “Rights Issue”). The subscription period ended on 26 November 2026. A total of 218,750,000 new ordinary shares, corresponding to approximately 69.2 percent of the ordinary shares offered, were subscribed for in the Rights Issue. Of these, 121,075,411 ordinary shares were subscribed for by virtue of subscription rights and 97,674,589 ordinary shares were subscribed for without exercising subscription rights, of which 88,638,814 ordinary shares were subscribed for pursuant to the underwriting commitment. The Rights Issue will provide the Company with proceeds of approximately 175 MSEK before deduction of issue costs.

Outcome of the Rights Issue

The Rights Issue comprised a maximum of 316,143,504 new ordinary shares at a subscription price of SEK 0.80 per ordinary share. A total of 121,075,411 ordinary shares, corresponding to approximately 38.3 percent of the ordinary shares offered, have been subscribed for by virtue of subscription rights. In addition, applications for subscription of 9,035,775 ordinary shares without exercising subscription rights have been received, corresponding to approximately 2.9 percent of the ordinary shares offered.

The allotment to those who applied for subscription without exercising subscription rights, excluding the underwriter, amounts to 9,035,775 ordinary shares, corresponding to approximately 2.9 percent of the ordinary shares offered. In addition, DNB Bank ASA (“DNB Bank”) has, pursuant to its underwriting commitment, subscribed for 88,638,814 ordinary shares, corresponding to approximately 28.0 percent of the ordinary shares offered. The underwriting commitment is therefore utilised in an amount of 70.9 MSEK.

The Rights Issue was covered by subscription commitments of approximately 16.0 MSEK and an underwriting commitment from DNB Bank of approximately 159.0 MSEK, amounting to a total of approximately 175 MSEK. DNB Bank’s underwriting commitment only covers subscription to the extent required for the Rights Issue to be subscribed up to this amount. Accordingly, the underwriting commitment does not cover subscription up to the full amount of the Rights Issue.

After deduction of estimated cash issue costs of approximately 30 MSEK, the Rights Issue is expected to provide the Company with net proceeds of approximately 145 MSEK, assuming that the underwriting fee is paid entirely in cash.

Allotment of shares subscribed for without exercising subscription rights

Allotment of ordinary shares subscribed for without exercising subscription rights is made in accordance with the principles set out in the Board of Directors’ resolution relating to the Rights Issue. Settlement notes will be sent on or around 30 November 2026 to those who have been allotted shares. No confirmation will be sent to those who have not been allotted shares. Payment for allotted ordinary shares must be made no later than 3 December 2026 in accordance with the instructions on the settlement note. Shareholders whose holdings are nominee-registered will be notified of allotment in accordance with the procedures of their respective nominees.

Shares and share capital

As a result of the Rights Issue, the total number of shares will increase from 37,156,639 to 255,906,639, of which 253,877,056 are ordinary shares and 2,029,583 are class C shares. The number of ordinary shares will increase from 35,127,056 to 253,877,056. The share capital will increase by SEK 89,624,993.299507, from SEK 15,223,604.669290 to SEK 104,848,597.968797. The Company holds all class C shares, which did not entitle the holder to subscription rights in the Rights Issue. The information above does not include any ordinary shares issued as payment of the underwriting fee.

For shareholders who did not participate in the Rights Issue, this corresponds to a dilution of approximately 86.2 percent, calculated as the number of new ordinary shares in the Rights Issue in relation to the total number of ordinary shares following the Rights Issue, excluding the Company’s own class C shares and assuming that the underwriting fee is paid entirely in cash.

Underwriting fee

The underwriting fee is payable either in cash at 13.0 percent of the underwritten amount or, at the election of the underwriter, in the form of newly issued ordinary shares corresponding to 15.0 percent of the underwritten amount, on the same terms and conditions as the shares in the Rights Issue, including the subscription price of SEK 0.80 per ordinary share. DNB Bank has stated that the form of the fee will reflect the respective choices of its sub-underwriters. The fee is calculated on the underwritten amount and not on the amount for which the underwriting commitment is actually utilised.

If the underwriting fee is to be paid in the form of newly issued ordinary shares, the Company will announce the resolution regarding such issue, including the number of ordinary shares, through a separate press release.

DNB Bank is the parent company of DNB Carnegie Investment Bank AB (publ) (“DNB Carnegie”), which acts as Sole Global Coordinator and Sole Bookrunner in connection with the Rights Issue.

Registration and trading

The last day of trading in paid subscribed shares (BTA) is expected to be 3 December 2026. The new ordinary shares covered by the initial registration are expected to be admitted to trading on Nasdaq Stockholm on or around 9 December 2026. Please note that trading may commence before or after this date, depending on the procedures applied by individual banks and nominees.

Lock-up undertakings

In connection with the Rights Issue, the Company has entered into a lock-up undertaking pursuant to which the Company’s Board of Directors may not propose or resolve on any new share issues during a period of 180 days from the date of announcement of the outcome of the Rights Issue, subject to customary exceptions, including the implementation of incentive programmes. DNB Carnegie may grant exemptions from the lock-up undertaking.

In addition, Novo Holdings A/S and the Company’s Board of Directors and management have entered into lock-up undertakings for a period of 180 days from the date of announcement of the outcome of the Rights Issue. The undertakings cover shares and other securities in the Company that are held or acquired and are subject to customary exceptions and the specific exceptions previously communicated in respect of Novo Holdings A/S, including the possibility to carry out certain block trades. DNB Carnegie may grant exemptions from the lock-up undertakings.

Advisers

DNB Carnegie Investment Bank AB (publ) acts as Sole Global Coordinator and Sole Bookrunner in connection with the Rights Issue. Advokatfirman Vinge is legal adviser to Orexo.
